homeTitle: Learn the Dhamma with Win Metta
homeIntro: Win Metta is a nonprofit community that preserves and shares Theravāda Buddhist teachings in Burmese and English. This site is a free place to find Dhamma books and study resources. No account is needed.
homeLibraryText: Search and browse thousands of Dhamma books and study materials in PDF, most of them in Burmese.

aboutIntro: Win Metta is a USA-based California 501(c)(3) nonprofit that preserves and shares Theravāda Buddhist teachings in Burmese and English. We serve learners in Myanmar and around the world.
aboutWork1: Dhamma teaching and meditation instruction in Burmese and English, including guided retreats.
aboutWork2: Pāḷi scripture and Burmese language classes, so more people can read the classical texts.
aboutWork3: Technology and administrative support for monastic communities.
aboutTeachers: Our classes and teachings come from Sayadaws and Venerable monks based in California, Arizona, Myanmar and elsewhere. We share their teachings as given and do not rewrite them.
aboutFree: The Dhamma Library and our teaching materials are free to use, without an account or payment.
aboutMore: More about Win Metta on winmetta.org
privacyIntro: This page explains what this site does with your information. It describes how the site works today.
privacyNone: This site has no accounts, no advertising and no tracking cookies,. We use cookieless analytics (see "Website analytics" below). Searching and filtering the catalog happen in your browser, and typing a search does not send it to us. See "Search words in the page address" below for one exception.
privacyAnalytics: We count visits so that we can see which pages, classes, retreats, library folders, books and Dhamma posts are used, and in which languages. We use Umami, software that we run ourselves on our own server (hosted with Amazon Web Services in the United States), so no analytics company receives this data. The counting uses no cookies and stores nothing on your device. It does not collect your name, e-mail address, the words you search for, or anything you type. Umami uses your IP address to estimate your location and calculate a session code that changes each day. Umami does not use that code to link sessions across days. Our analytics server may record IP addresses in error logs when a request fails. Like any website, we can see the country, region and city (estimated from your IP address), browser, operating system, device type, browser language and time of day that come with each visit, and the website that linked you here (only its address, not the page), but only as totals. We keep the counts for at most 13 months. If your browser sends Do Not Track, we do not count your visit.
privacyAnalyticsIp: For troubleshooting and traffic analysis, Win Metta records the full IP address in private Caddy access logs for the analytics server and on individual Umami sessions. The access logs include request time, method, route category, status and duration. Authorized maintainers can see the IP address and use it to compare activity across sessions. Live IP records are kept for up to seven days during normal operation. Database dumps expire after 21 days and volume snapshots expire after 14 days, so backup copies can remain after the live IP record is removed. Our tracker does not send analytics requests when your browser signals Do Not Track.
privacyStored: If you choose a language, or the languages you read Dhamma posts in, your browser remembers that choice on your device (opening a shared post link that names its languages also sets it) so the site can offer it next time, and opening the site's main address goes straight to your language. The Settings page changes or clears these choices. It is not sent anywhere. If your browser blocks this storage, the site works the same and you can still change language.
privacyHosting: This site's pages and PDF files are delivered by hosting and content delivery providers (currently Amazon Web Services CloudFront for pages and bunny.net for PDF files) and, for website analytics, by our own analytics server at stats.app.winmetta.org, hosted with Amazon Web Services. Like any web service, they process technical information such as your IP address and which pages and files you request, in order to deliver them and keep them secure. See the website analytics section for how we use technical information for analytics.
privacyLinks: Some links lead to other websites, such as winmetta.org. Their privacy practices are their own.

retreatsHowOnsite: In-person retreats are held in a monastery. The Sayadaw leads the meditation sessions, and Win Metta volunteers take care of the logistics. Yogis who cannot travel can often join over Zoom.

privacySearchUrlTitle: Search words in the page address
privacySearchUrl: While you search or filter, the site adds your search words, filters and chosen time zone to the page address (for example ?q=…) so that you can bookmark or share the page and use the Back button. The address stays in your browser as you type. But when you open, reload or share such a link, the address is requested from the hosting provider like any other page address, so your search words can appear in its request logs. Please do not put personal information in a search, and share a link only if you are comfortable with its words being visible.

privacyFeedback: When you send feedback, your message, the page and item you report, its language and your interface language are emailed to the Win Metta team through Amazon SNS. Your email address is optional and used only to answer you. Please leave out personal details. Reports are not saved in an application database or request logs; they remain in the recipients’ mailboxes. Opening the form and submitting it send anonymous counts of the context, problem type and success, never the message or email address. The Sādhu button, when available, counts anonymous appreciation clicks. No cookie or storage key is added for either feature. Do Not Track disables these anonymous counts.

privacyBookSearch: When you use the search inside PDFs, the words you type are sent to a Win Metta search service on Amazon Web Services, which finds the matching pages. The words are used only to answer that search: they are not saved, not written to logs and not sent to analytics. Like any web service, Amazon Web Services handles your IP address to deliver the answer; Win Metta does not log or keep it. Analytics records only that a PDF search happened, the number of results as a range and the script of the words (Burmese, Latin or mixed), and Do Not Track disables these anonymous counts. Searching titles and tags stays in your browser.
donateIntro: Win Metta keeps the Dhamma free: classes, retreats, study groups and the Dhamma Library have no fees, no paywall and no login. Your dāna pays for what it takes to offer them, and for the monastics and teachers who give the teachings.
donateSupportClassesTitle: Online classes, retreats and study groups
donateSupportClasses: Zoom meetings for weekly classes, retreats and study groups, and Restream to share teachings live with students who cannot join the meeting.
donateSupportWebsite: Hosting on AWS for this website, the Dhamma Library books and the search inside them, and the network that delivers files quickly around the world, along with the websites, apps and online services we build next.
donateSupportVolunteersTitle: Teaching materials and tools for volunteers
donateSupportVolunteers: Canva for class slides and notices; Google Workspace for email, shared files and forms; 1Password to keep the organization’s accounts safe; and AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT that help volunteers prepare slides, translations and summaries. The teachers’ words are never changed. Win Metta is run by volunteers, and these tools let them do careful work in a few spare hours.
donateSupportMonastics: Support for the Sayadaws, monasteries and Dhamma teachers in the USA and abroad who teach in our classes, and for meditation retreats.

aboutDana: Win Metta has no fees. Donations pay for Zoom and the other online services behind our classes, retreats and study groups, for hosting this website and the Dhamma Library, for the tools volunteers use, and for the Sayadaws and teachers who teach.
